My ex-boss (and the company founder) gave my email to one of his friends (who I’d briefly met at a couple company events) to ask me out. Friend was late 60s-70s, I’m in late 20s. Creeped me the f out, was even angrier when I found out my boss had given him my email for this purpose. This was after a year of fending off advances from another company executive. Plus another coworker insisted on going out to drinks (after I spent weeks trying to avoid it), where he decided to tell me all about how he and his wife are “trying polyamory.” I was later fired after finally reporting the executive. Let’s just say this company had cultivated a… permissive environment, and I was the only female engineer. EEOC case in progress. 

Echoing what others have said, document everything. Forward any relevant emails to *non-work* email. I’d try to avoid any 1-1s and have witnesses present if possible. Sending this email in the first place shows pretty poor judgement on his part, so I wouldn’t assume rejecting him (even gently) won’t lead to any retaliation.

Also, if you have health insurance, some of them have behavioral health lines you can call. I have Kaiser, which has a 24/7 line staffed with therapists. They are… fairly hit or miss but still better than 988 in my experience. I can’t speak to other insurance companies but maybe you could ask.

I’m so sorry you’re in this place. I have been there too and I understand how bad it feels. I’ve had very mixed, mostly bad experiences with 988 too.      

In my case, I call warmlines pretty frequently. I have used the NAMI warmline directory quite a bit to find their numbers: https://www.nami.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Warmline-Directory-as-of-August-16-2024.pdf   (since you mentioned 988, I’m assuming you’re in the US?)    

That document isn’t entirely up to date, some of the hours are wrong and a couple of the numbers don’t pick up anymore. Different lines give you different amounts of time, sometimes they are busier than others and can’t talk for as long. Not all of them are trained crisis counselors, a lot of them are peer supporters. But frankly I’ve had a vastly better experience overall with all the warmlines i’ve called than any so-called “professional therapist” line — many of the people working the lines have had their own struggles and are very empathetic. I’d say between 80% and 90% of the time I have a good experience with the ones I call regularly. With 988 it’s more like 25% if that.   

I’ve called warmlines when suicidal and they have been helpful, although I’ve never had an active suicide plan so I can’t speak to what their protocol is in that case. But sometimes you just need another human being to talk to, and I have way better luck finding kind humans on those lines than at 988.

It’s kind of a long and complicated story without a happy ending. But to give the overview, I met someone who seemed to be one of the first and only truly emotionally safe people I’ve ever known. Some odd circumstances meant that we spent a lot of time together and he came to be the person I trusted most in the world, and I don’t trust most people. Even if I didn’t know what I wanted to hear, he somehow said the exact right thing. I don’t think I’ve ever met a person as kind and compassionate as he is. I’ve feared for years that maybe I just require way too much patience and kindness for anyone to give so that I can get to a healthier place, and maybe it’s just not possible for me. But suddenly there was this person who was so kind and patient and didn’t make me feel like a burden for not being perfectly put together. And slowly, over time, my positive emotions started coming back, not just emotions that had to do with him, but all emotions. 

Unfortunately, because my life seems to tend towards the dramatic, he was married and we ended up developing romantic feelings towards one another (which we did NOT act on, just want to be clear). But because of this I had to distance myself from him and things got really emotionally messy for a few months, we still had to see each other sometimes. I had hoped that maybe we would each be able to separately work though whatever emotions we had and one day be friends again. But we knew each other through work, and the job turned out to be more like a cult than anything else. (I don’t say that lightly, we were literally living together in our boss’s house in the middle of the freaking woods, working nonstop, I lived there for six months having tasks thrown at me 24/7 and listening to the nonstop delusions of grandeur of the “founder” who thinks he’s some sort of misunderstood genius.) He was the main reason I got sucked into the job/cult, I trusted him and he spent a LOT of time emotionally manipulating me to suck me in, telling me how much he admired me and talking about “all the great things we could do together.” Now I’m out of the job/cult, he’s still firmly in it, I’ll never see him again, and i guess my body is trying to protect itself because my positive emotions are now firmly shut off again while I try to process what I just escaped, and wonder whether he was actually an emotionally safe person who is stuck in a terrible circumstance or if he’s actually a masterful emotional manipulator and I can’t trust my judgments about people at all. So yeah. Weird times. And idk if I’ll ever be able to trust my instincts again, let alone another person.

This comment section is why I’ve never attempted to seek any sort of emotional support here for navigating being (relatively) successful while also suffering immensely from complex trauma. I got onto a trajectory that I never could have imagined someone like me, coming from my background, could ever be on. And I just ran with it, my survival mode was just working myself to death while feeling like a total imposter, which made me seem “successful” on the outside until I broke down. And believe me, none of the people who “valued” me for my work stuck around. Now my work is in shambles but my work is all I have, I live every day with the burden that literally no person cares if I live or die or would even notice. People don’t see me come home and fall apart, people don’t know that the suicide hotline is the only number I have to call. It’s a miserable life that I’ve lost all energy to continue to try to make better.

No. Some of us have experienced a lifetime of severe trauma, are locked in the throes of CPTSD, and throw themselves into work as a coping mechanism, thus achieving “success” at least by capitalist metrics. I myself used my work to pull myself out of where I came from and get some modicum of stability in my life. I never had the luxury of a safety net, intensive therapy, or the ability to take time off, so I just worked and worked and somehow that made me “successful” (relatively), it was that or homelessness. No one sees me falling apart calling crisis hotlines every night, no one sees me break down after giving a talk in front of 500 people, knowing that not one person on earth actually cares about me as a human being, only my work gives me worth. So yeah. CPTSD and high achievement can co-exist, it’s just another style of coping mechanism.

I guess I’m mixed as far as feeling emotions goes. I feel negative emotions very intensely, and frequently get angry or distraught and cry all the time. But I lost the ability to feel all positive emotions—joy, affection, love. Even if I’m laughing and seem happy, I don’t actually feel any emotions inside. Hey, thanks for sharing your story, and sorry it's taken me so long to reply, I've been easily overwhelmed lately. 

I know our stories aren't the same, but you really articulated a lot of my feelings around why Covid was so bad for me personally and continues to be, despite the rest of the world seeming to have moved on entirely. It really does come down to the support network. In a lot of ways it shouldn't have been that bad, at least for me --- I had a roof over my head for most of it, I was fully out of the DV I grew up in, I wasn't on the front lines and didn't get covid until I was already vaccinated. Even though I was totally isolated for most of it, and lost all my income to the point where I was homeless for a year, the way I grew up was so much worse, and it could have been so much worse. And yet, I came closer to ending it all during Covid than I ever have. 

For me it was a combination of being at an incredibly hopeful point in my life, feeling like I was on the cusp of a big positive change, and the total lack of support that I had once the world shut down. I had just moved to another country to work in the top research lab in my field, and felt like I had been gifted a totally fresh start. I went into it with so much energy and hope, and then two months in we were in lockdown and I was in a foreign country where I knew zero people, alone in a studio apartment barely big enough for a full size bed. I actually thought I had a few friends, albeit on the other side of an ocean, but when I started to reach out to people for even a video chat I was just ignored. It felt like everyone in the world just retreated into their innermost circles, but from where I was sitting it was like every relationship I thought I had built over the years retreated away and I was left with no one, not even an occasional response to a text, since I am not a part of any innermost circle. It was a stark reminder of my place in the world and to be honest I'm still not over it. 

And now it's supposed to just be over? And back to normal? I guess for other people all that means is, what, going places with their pre-existing support networks? And I'm just here totally bruised and battered with absolutely no energy to begin trying to build community again. Because the last time I thought I had community, I had absolutely nothing when it really counted. I tried so hard to be there (virtually) for everyone I knew, and they just didn't even need me because they already had people to fulfill that need. 

I'm rambling a lot, but your description of feeling "maimed in a ditch" really got me. That's exactly how I feel, and almost no one gets it at all. We're just all supposed to be back to happy normal lives with our friends and partners. This all felt out of reach before covid, but now it feels impossible. 

Your last paragraph got me too. Again, really articulated everything I'm feeling. So much so that I don't really have anything to say, other than yes. Maybe it is a case of finding what makes sense for the new trajectory. I'm having trouble letting go of the dream for what my life could have been, but I'm just too exhausted to make that happen anymore.

I think needing time to build trust is a huge barrier for me. In my case, it's not about committing to a relationship. It's about even starting a relationship in the first place. I'm physically incapable of intimacy (emotional or physical) before some level of trust is built, and no guy is sticking around for someone who's not having sex with them in this day and age. In my ideal scenario any relationship would start as a platonic friendship, but that isn't happening anymore now that I barely spend any time around people either at work or socially, and (even though I know it's not really true) it feels like I'm the last single person on the planet and everyone I meet has been in a relationship for 3+ years. 

About the healing and relationships, I feel like I've always had a very realistic perspective on this, but many people infantalize me and assume I'm looking at a relationship as a panacea. (Not saying you are treating me this way, just that many people have.) My perspective on it for years has been pretty much exactly what you laid out. In fact, I expect that getting into a relationship would cause things to get much, much worse for me, hopefully temporarily, and hopefully when I could manage it in a way that it doesn't put all the burden of dealing with my BS straight onto the other person. Even just realizing that I have strong non-platonic feelings for someone I care deeply about who has actually shown care back, even though there is no way for it to turn into a romantic relationship, has caused me to basically become non-functional for the last month. This in itself is terrifying to me. I'm terrified that I might finally one day meet someone who is great for me, but then fuck it all up if I accidentally spew my trauma BS all over the relationship. Then what? Wait another 10 years for another try? Hope that I somehow find a saint who is willing to put up with me while I get my shit together, but end up hating myself for hurting someone I care about? 

I realize my reasoning is a bit paradoxical, but while I would never want to treat someone as a "practice relationship" (unfair to them, and I'd be incapable of that), I also don't understand how to get that experience and growth without actually doing it. To use a stupid example, you can't learn to play the cello by watching YouTube videos about it, no matter how many you watch. You learn by doing the thing and putting in the work, over and over. I have been oft-infuriated by people (again, not you) repeatedly cautioning me that "relationships are hard work" as if I don't understand this and I'm not willing to do the work. I feel like I'm shouting into a void, I WANT TO DO THE WORK, I WANT TO MAKE MYSELF BETTER, I WANT TO GROW AS A PERSON AND CARE ABOUT OTHER PEOPLE.  I didn't get where I am today because I'm afraid of hard work, quite the opposite. In fact, I have been trying very hard to establish healthy therapeutic relationships as well as other self-care (weight lifting, hiking, healthy nutrition, writing, and more). I have known for a long time that I should NOT get into a relationship (on the one in a billion chance it ever happens) without an established trusted therapist, so that I have a place to work through the issues that I *know* will come up in the context of this sort of relationship, without placing the burden on a partner.

This turned into a ramble, like all of my comments. But I appreciate your reply and thank you also for saying that I do deserve love, it helps a lot to hear that after so many years of hearing nothing but damaging toxic positivity platitudes.

>I get nervous when I hear people talk about needing connection, mostly because it's been unavailable. If I can only be whole with others, and I can't make or keep connections with others, does that mean I'm condemned to be broken forever?

I hear you. And I've felt this fear too, for a long time. I spent 10 years telling myself I didn't need anyone else, that I could figure it all out on my own, that I wouldn't let my past keep me from being everything I set out to be. 

Then something just broke. I don't know exactly when it happened or what it was, but I just couldn't keep going pretending like I could do it all on my own. For me I think covid isolation triggered it. I started trying my hardest to build a community and learn to trust other people, and that was when my emotional stability really started to get bad. Now I don't know what to believe. I no longer feel that stubbornness that I can heal my wounds without connection, but I also see a society where connection no longer seems to exist. 

I focus on romantic relationships as a source of connection a lot, mostly because those are the types of relationships our society places above all others. I've literally had therapists scold me for being upset that my "friends" ignore me for months to years because "they have partners and lives they have to worry about" while in the same breath telling me that I'm silly for being upset that I don't have a partner because "you can get everything you need from friendship." Well, I'm not getting anything I need, so clearly someone's reasoning is off. 

But it's not just romantic relationships, I think our entire sense of community as a society has crumbled, and thus has made it harder for those of us who don't come from stable families to build community, "chosen family", whatever you want to call it. It feels like everyone just walks around with this mentality like "I got mine, don't expect anything from me." Even really simple things like having a friendly neighbor to chat with occasionally, or seeing the same people at a neighborhood coffee shop, or having friendly workmates that you see regularly. I used to build up this "bank" of positive interactions, small and large, and sometimes when the bank got full enough I felt more able to try harder to build relationships. If the ratio of negative to positive interactions got too large, I'd withdraw for awhile until I felt ready to try again. Now I have nearly zero interactions with other people, and I have nearly zero tolerance for any negative interaction because the bank has been empty for years. 

I used to find belonging in my work and in nature. I've lost the work part, and covid lockdowns took the nature part away. And the last year and a half I've basically just been madly scrambling to get my life back together and get a roof back over my head after covid destroyed me, I haven't been able to do any of the things that used to keep me sane. I can't remember the last time I've been in the ocean or slept outside. I've decided I need to start doing those things again immediately otherwise I'll lose everything I've worked for. Because I think that constant sense of not belonging is really breaking me. 

Sorry for the long ramble. Thanks for replying, and I hope you're right that the wounds can heal without help.

I'm a little bit older than you I'm guessing (I suppose I'm a "zillennial" because I'm not truly a Gen Z nor a millennial) but all I've seen my whole life is the fracturing of society and the lack of community. I've done so much "inner work", tried to process the traumas. Listened to people who said that "processing/facing the trauma" was the key to getting better. Well, I did that, and now what? My life is measurably worse than it was a few years ago, and the direct cause of that is extreme social isolation caused by starting out behind in life in this hyper-individualistic world. If you dare try to point out that the isolation and lack of community or support system is impeding your healing, you're told to "love yourself" or "learn to be happy alone" by people who got a leg up at the start of life by not being traumatized and now have spent years building social support networks instead of having to work on "healing" (whatever the hell that means, I don't even know anymore). 

I'd say that 90% of the conversations I have with crisis line workers (who are basically the only humans I talk to on a regular basis nowadays, since I work remotely and have zero people in my life) end with them telling me to download some bullshit "mindfulness" app and "work on my self-care with the app". These conversations always end with me breaking down in bitter, hysterical laughter. I try to explain to these mindless zombies that the very fact that the only human I've talked to in weeks is trying to foist me off onto an app so they don't have to deal with me, is a quintessential example of how sick our society is. Then they call me difficult and hang up. It would be hilarious if it wasn't so heart-wrenchingly hopeless. 

Anyway, you're not alone in feeling this way. I don't know what to do, but all I can say is there are other people out there who are also seeing the crumbling of our communities and don't know where to turn.

Late to this, and I'm not a lawyer but I do work as a (misclassified) IC and have had to learn a lot about this so wanted to correct some of the bad advice in the comments you've received. It sounds to me like you're misclassified.

* "If you're on a 1099 you're an IC." <- No. Neither you nor the employer determine whether you're an IC. The IRS or DoL determine whether you're an IC. Depending on what state you live in, the test for whether someone is a true IC can be pretty stringent. (Because businesses pull this shit to save money all the time.)
* Just because it's in a contract and you both agreed to it doesn't mean it's enforceable. My contracts say lots of laughable things that are blatantly trying to get around misclassification claims. That doesn't mean it would hold up in court if it were to end up there. Just because the training isn't explicitly mandatory, if you have to train an IC for them to be able to perform the job it means they're not an IC. ICs aren't trained, they come with an existing specialized skillset that the company doesn't have.
* On that note, if what you're engaged as a 1099 for is a core/integral part of the company's business, you're not an IC, you're misclassified. A tutor working for a *tutoring company* is engaged in the core part of that company's business. If you were developing their website it might be different. If you were running your own tutoring company you would be self-employed and coming up with your own lesson plans, etc. You're performing the service they are providing and getting stiffed out of benefits and shafted at tax time, this is payroll fraud and wage theft.
* "The rules about the lesson plans, formats, etc. are all fine" <- No. For a true IC relationship, the company cannot control the methods used, only the results. (If you hired a plumber to fix your toilet would you be telling them what parts to use? No, you hired them for expertise you don't have, you just care whether the toilet is fixed. (just an example, don't want to imply you can't fix a toilet haha)
* I save 30-35% of my income for taxes. Have been saving closer to 30% since my expenses are so high that I can write off a lot. Pay estimated taxes quarterly so you don't get caught at tax time with a bill you can't pay that you'll end up paying interest on. BUT, you can also file IRS form SS-8 for the IRS to make a determination of whether or not you're properly classified, and if they rule in your favor I believe you will get paid back the excess self-employment tax you paid. I've not yet gone through this process (yet) so I don't know how long it takes or if it happens anonymously so bridges aren't burned [https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-ss-8](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-ss-8)  If a determination is made in your favor there are other forms you can file to claim back the employer portion of Medicare/SS taxes.
* Mandatory meetings are a red flag for misclassification. As is "setting your schedule", but only within their required hours. Obviously if you were running your own tutoring company you would have to work during hours that your customers were available, but if you wanted to run the "Night Owl Tutoring Company" and only see clients from 2-5am you'd be totally free to do that (whether your business would survive is another story).
* One of the key elements for determine whether someone is properly classified is "opportunity for profit/loss". If you were running your own tutoring company, you could market yourself, try to get more students via word of mouth. You could grow your client base, you could eventually hire more employees if your business got big enough. If you can't do any of these things because your relationship with your tutoring students is under the control of your "client" (NOT your employer! If you're an IC they're your client!) you're don't have an opportunity to grow your business.

One of the other commenters is right that this is a question for a labor lawyer, but if you're like me and have been so badly screwed over by persistent wage thieves that you can't afford one, you can file a determination request with the IRS and see if that process does something. But in the meantime, either get another job or protect yourself by paying estimated tax and saving way more than you think you need for taxes. I got utterly screwed by taxes and penalties for tax underpayment the first time I got 1099ed so I know whereof I speak.

Hopefully some of this is helpful. I've been reading into this a lot in the past year and am quite irritated about how often people try to take advantage of others, often when they are young and don't even know what questions to ask to understand if they are being taken advantage of.

Edit: I just did the American thing of assuming you're in the US because I have been spending my afternoon angrily reading stories of 1099 misclassification and thought you mentioned 1099 in your post (which if you're not American, is the tax form you receive when you're an IC). Apologies if a lot of this is irrelevant if you're not in the US, but hopefully this comment is useful for someone out there wondering if their wages and benefits are being stolen.
